posts.text:
“Verify” is a little loose yeah. In practice, it has been pretty useful for Claude to do something like:

1. Build a model of the program, targeting a tricky state machine or race-prone part of the code
2. Find counter-examples in the model: these are suspected bugs 
3. Reproduce the bugs
4. Fix the bugs

@elonmusk @fchollet That's what my book is about that came out today. The Eureka Machine, where I explain how to build such an invention generating AI system and show that we're already making progress towards it. 

https://t.co/TOdiVDkolY

quotedTweet.text:
AI moves so fast that I thought this book was going to be a year too late. It turns out it's right on time.

While I was writing, I kept having to change chapters from "someone should do this" to "someone has done this," and then go talk to the people who had done it. A good example is the chapter on virtual cells. I'd written that we needed large initiatives to build one. By the time I finished, I was writing about the ones that exist — the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative's is now the largest and best-funded push to model a human cell.

The Eureka Machine is out today.

It's about building a full-stack scientific superintelligence: a living map of human knowledge, a model of physical reality, high-fidelity simulations, autonomous labs, and an agent swarm of AI scientists on top. There's no better science to start with than the science of AI itself, because that's where the feedback loop is tightest. Then you expand the aperture to physics, chemistry, and especially pre-clinical biology.

This will be the most meaningful application of AI, and one of the most important things humanity does. And it may be the last organic invention we need to make. After that, it starts inventing everything else for us to solve our most pressing problems.

While writing, I couldn't let the idea go. Eight of us started @Recursive_SI to go build it.

AI is going to massively accelerate science, and unlike most of what gets argued about right now, that isn't zero sum.

I hope you all enjoy the book. I look forward to discussing it with you all.
quotedTweet.translationZh:
AI 发展太快，我原以为这本书会晚一年。结果它来得正是时候。

写作期间，我不断得把章节从“应该有人做这件事”改成“已经有人做了这件事”，然后去和那些已经做出来的人交流。虚拟细胞那章就是一个很好的例子。我原本写的是我们需要大型计划来构建一个虚拟细胞。等我写完时，我写的已经是现有项目了，其中 Chan Zuckerberg Initiative 如今是建模人类细胞规模最大、资金最充足的推进力量。

The Eureka Machine 今天发布。

它讲的是如何构建一个全栈科学超级智能：一张活的人类知识地图、一个物理现实模型、高保真模拟、自主实验室，以及位于其上的 AI 科学家智能体群。没有比 AI 科学本身更适合作为起点的科学了，因为这里的反馈循环最紧密。然后再把视野扩展到物理、化学，尤其是临床前生物学。

这将是 AI 最有意义的应用，也将是人类要做的最重要的事情之一。它也可能是我们需要完成的最后一项有机发明。之后，它会开始为我们发明其他一切，帮助解决最紧迫的问题。

写作过程中，我始终放不下这个想法。我们八个人创办了 @Recursive_SI，去把它造出来。

AI 将极大加速科学发展，而且不同于当下大多数争论的事情，这不是零和博弈。

希望大家喜欢这本书。期待和大家讨论。
